articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreak in northwest China involves serotype SAT1, confirmed by the Ministry of Agriculture as affecting cattle in Gansu and Xinjiang. Since late last weekend, large-scale disinfection and spraying have been conducted to salvage herds, and livestock markets in Xinjiang and Gansu have been temporarily closed. The SAT1 strain, originally African, has infected 219 of 6,229 cattle across the two provinces. Experts warn the virus is highly contagious and airborne, enabling rapid spread between farms. Authorities link entry to western border corridors near Kazakhstan, Mongolia, and Russia, and have tightened patrols to prevent smuggled animals. Reports of a similar outbreak in Siberia are unconfirmed and denied by Russia. Since 2025, SAT1 has moved from Africa toward the Middle East and Western Asia. Mortality in young cattle can exceed 50%, heightening farmer risk and containment pressure.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Dangerous parasite activates "crusher" to fool the human immune system.
articleHeadline: Parasita perigoso ativa "triturador" para enganar sistema imune humano
articleSummary: Trypanosoma brucei, the causative agent of sleeping sickness, employs a protein coat of Variant Surface Glycoproteins (VSG) to evade the human immune response. A new study in Nature Microbiology (2026) led by Lianne I.M. Lansink identifies ESB2, a key protein in the parasite’s protein-production center that acts as a highly selective RNA filter. As RNA is processed, ESB2 destroys specific transcripts, implementing an RNA destruction mechanism that shapes which proteins are ultimately expressed. This 'molecular shredder' explains longstanding imbalances in protein production and enhanced camouflage, enabling parasite persistence in blood, transmitted by the tsetse fly. Clinically, sleeping sickness can progress to severe central nervous system involvement, with sleep disturbances, confusion, and coma. Blocking ESB2 is proposed as a potential therapeutic target to disrupt survival and immune evasion.

articleSummary: Indonesia reports 1.09 million tuberculosis (TB) cases; 867,000 treated in the previous year, leaving almost 300,000 undetected. Deputy Health Minister Benjamin Paulus Octavianus announced this on World TB Day 2026 in Jakarta, underscoring a high TB burden. He said eradication requires cross-sector action beyond the Health Ministry, involving Kemendagri (Home Affairs), PKP (Public Works and Housing), Kemensos (Social Affairs), Kemenko Pangan (Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs), Kemenaker, and the Environment Ministry. A more expansive 2026 screening program will target reductions, especially among lower-income deciles 1–4. He warned that TB bacteria die in sunlight after 15–30 minutes in the air, but in poorly ventilated homes they can persist for months, emphasizing housing and ventilation improvements alongside case finding.

articleSummary: Measles outbreak response immunization (ORI) is underway in Klaten Regency, Indonesia, after public health authorities declared a health emergency (KLB) following several measles cases. articleHeadline: Phát hiện lao phổi sau hai tuần ho ra máu
articleSummary: Pulmonary tuberculosis diagnosed in Hanoi, Vietnam, in a 38-year-old woman, Ms. Hằng, after about two weeks of hemoptysis and productive sputum. Thoracic CT at Tam Anh General Hospital in Hanoi shows focal parenchymal lung lesions. Bronchial secretions tested by Xpert MTB/RIF were positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, confirming TB. Upon admission, rapid clinical deterioration with persistent hemoptysis and systemic weakness occurred. Initial labs showed elevated AST (48.1 U/L) with normal ALT (13.3 U/L) and hyperuricemia (1.5× upper limit). Suspected anti-TB–drug–induced hepatotoxicity led clinicians to temporarily pause certain agents and closely monitor liver function and uric acid. Once indices stabilized, anti-TB therapy was resumed with ongoing clinical surveillance; symptoms subsided, cough and sputum decreased, inflammatory markers fell, and liver function remained controlled. The patient was discharged with outpatient TB treatment. TB transmission occurs via respiratory droplets; early detection and treatment reduce transmission and improve prognosis, as symptoms may be absent despite disease.

articleSummary: Syphilis diagnosed in a male patient over 20 at Hanoi's Central Dermatology Hospital, Vietnam. He reported unprotected sex two weeks earlier, followed by penile lesions: white patches, swelling, and purulent discharge around the foreskin; initial self-treatment with betel leaf and unclear ointments preceded progression. After about a month, purulent drainage and mild itching appeared; no fever. Lab tests: rapid syphilis test positive; RPR 1:32; TPHA 1:20,480; Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci and gram-negative rods. Ultrasound: bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy, largest 16.6 x 5.4 mm. Diagnosis: syphilis, with possible co-infection. Treatment: single deep intramuscular benzathine penicillin 2,400,000 units and topical antibiotics. After 3 days, lesions cleaned, erosion improved, itching subsided. Syphilis caused by Treponema pallidum; transmitted primarily sexually; can affect skin, mucous membranes, and organs; complications include neurosyphilis, cardiovascular syphilis, congenital syphilis. Global ~7 million new adult cases/year; Vietnam 2–5% of STIs; 4.0% of STI patients; 4.5% among female sex workers. Emphasize early testing and safe sex; reinfection risk remains.

articleHeadline: Functional role of T-cell activation in viral hepatitis
articleSummary: HBV and HCV remain major global health concerns: approximately 350 million chronically HBV infected, mainly in East and Southeast Asia and Africa, and about 170 million HCV infections, with Egypt showing the highest prevalence. articleSummary: Tubercular lymphadenitis, a form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis, often presents as a painless neck swelling and can occur in the armpit or other sites, challenging recognition in India where TB affects non-lung sites. In Chhatarpur, rural and semi-urban areas, health workers have screened over 150,000 people across more than 320 villages, diagnosing more than 5,000 extrapulmonary TB cases, many first noticed as swelling. Diagnosis relies on FNAC (Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology), with biopsy or additional tests if needed. Once confirmed, anti-tubercular therapy is highly effective when adhered to; delayed or incomplete treatment risks progression and complications. The message: not every swelling is cancer; early detection and proper treatment can change outcomes.

articleSummary: A Chinese-led study published in Nature Microbiology links the nodavirus CMNV, traditionally infecting farmed shrimp, to a human ocular disease—uveitis with elevated intraocular pressure. In 70 patients with uveitis of unknown etiology, researchers detected CMNV particles in ocular tissues and found viral genomes 98.96% identical to marine-animal CMNV; incubation estimated at 6–12 months. Epidemiology shows over 70% of human cases tied to raw seafood consumption or close contact with seafood handlers, with frequent marine-animal contact markedly increasing risk. CMNV was found in 351 marine-animal samples sold at markets, including fish, shrimp, crabs, and mollusks. Ecological screening indicates global distribution, strongest in Antarctica (35.5%), Africa (20.4%), and the Americas and Asia (~16.4% each). The virus circulated in 27.7% of farmed and 32.8% of wild animal populations. Experts, including ichthyologist Yuri Simakov, warn the pathogen could pose pandemic potential and advocates for monitoring.

articleHeadline: When the needle drops: What Bangladesh's measles crisis tells us about India's public health discipline
articleSummary: Bangladesh faced a measles surge in 2026, reporting nearly 700 confirmed cases in the first three months and at least 50 child deaths as hospitals run on corridors and stairs. The outbreak follows years of administrative missteps—procurement delays during political transition, a 2024 measles-rubella catch-up campaign cancellation amid civil unrest, and healthcare worker protests—producing an immunity debt once the virus found unprotected communities. Measles has an R0 of 12–18, requiring >95% herd immunity to contain spread. By contrast, India reports high, sustained vaccination coverage: first-dose 97.8%, second-dose 93.3%; 2024 saw a 73% drop in measles cases and ongoing elimination efforts, aided by four decades of a stable Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP). articleHeadline: MF59-adjuvanted A/Astrakhan influenza vaccine induces cross-neutralizing H5N1 antibodies in ferrets against circulating clade 2.3.4.4b viruses - npj Vaccines
articleSummary: MF59-adjuvanted, egg-derived A/Astrakhan/3212/2020 (H5N8) vaccine (CBER-RG8A) elicited cross-neutralizing antibodies against circulating A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses in ferrets. A single dose yielded neutralizing GMTs ≥160; a second dose boosted titers by ≥3.3-fold. Cross-reactivity persisted across most strains, though responses were reduced up to 8-fold for strains with A156T HA mutation creating a potential glycosylation site at antigenic site B. Responses against divergent clades were limited, with modest titers against clade 2.3.2.1a. The data suggest broad protection against contemporary clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) viruses and highlight the value of ferret immunogenicity data to guide strain selection and regulatory preparedness when human clinical data are unavailable. The Salmonella strain involved is resistant to first-line antibiotics, complicating treatment; infections (salmonellosis) typically present 12–72 hours after ingestion with diarrhea, fever, and abdominal cramps, lasting about 4–7 days. High-risk groups include children under 5, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals. Anvisa notes the resistant subtype cannot be treated with conventional antibiotics and may require potent drugs in severe cases. In Brazil, moringa-based products have been prohibited since 2019 (safety concerns: genotoxic and hepatotoxic risks) and lack food approval. The ban aims to prevent import, sale, distribution, or use; no confirmed commercial imports have been identified, though online ads exist and personal imports cannot be ruled out.

articleHeadline: Sarampo preocupa profissionais da saúde, mas retorno pode ser evitado
articleSummary: Measles concerns health professionals as Brazil faces imported cases and a regional upsurge. Between 2025 and the second week of 2026, PAHO reported 15,922 measles cases in the Americas, with nearly 95% in the United States, Mexico, and Canada ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. In Brazil, 38 measles cases were recorded in 2025 and two in 2026, all imported, with Bolivia cited as the source of recent Brazilian infections. Although Brazil eliminated measles in 2016 and again in 2024, reintroduction risk persists because national two-dose coverage of the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine has not reached 95%. Prevention hinges on higher vaccination (including adults with irregular schedules), strengthened surveillance, and rapid response to suspected cases. The National Immunization Program (PNI) has intensified campaigns and ring vaccination; Campos Lindos in Tocantins accounted for about 60% of 2025 cases, guiding targeted interventions, aided by Zé Gotinha.

Control relies on farm sanitation, pest control, and rapid case identification. Treatment under a veterinarian may include Tilosin ST (tilosina, sulfadimidine, trimethoprim) via feed, leveraging synergistic effects against enteric bacteria.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Should a person who experiences an adverse event undergo laboratory tests such as serology or RT-PCR for dengue?
articleHeadline: A pessoa que tiver evento adverso deve realizar exames laboratoriais como sorologia ou RT-PCR para dengue?
articleSummary: Dengue laboratory testing is not automatic for adverse events after dengue vaccination; decisions depend on clinical evaluation and the suspected diagnosis. When there is a temporal association suggesting dengue related to vaccination, Technical Note 6/2026-CGFAM/DPNI/SVSA/MS from Brazil's health authorities directs laboratory investigations to confirm or exclude dengue infection and to consider other etiologies. Serology and NS1 antigen results must be interpreted with caution because the dengue vaccine is a live attenuated virus and can elicit immunobiological responses that yield reactive results, especially in serology. When indicated and within the appropriate diagnostic window, investigations should prioritize direct detection of the virus by RT-PCR; if dengue virus is detected, genetic sequencing may be necessary to differentiate wild-type virus from a possible vaccine-origin virus. This guidance supports targeted testing within Brazilian public health practice as of 6 April 2026.

articleSummary: Leprosy diagnosis in Brazil could be accelerated using a blood test for Mce1A antibodies combined with an AI-enhanced Leprosy Suspicion Questionnaire (LSQ/MaLeSQs). articleHeadline: 20-Year Study Reveals Cholera's Surprising Weakness
articleSummary: Cholera (Vibrio cholerae) in South Asia shows bacteria repeatedly gain/lose ICP1 phage defenses in the Ganges Basin (Bangladesh, North India). Two-decade genomic study of >2,300 genomes reveals phage ICP1 drives selection; defense maintenance yields milder disease and limited spread, while loss of defenses correlates with more severe illness and broader transmission. This challenges the idea that the Ganges Delta alone is the global source; the broader Ganges Basin appears to be the main source during the study period. In Bangladesh and North India, V. cholerae 7PET O1 originates near the Bay of Bengal and remains often within national borders, influenced by human movement and population density. The work suggests phage-based therapies and genomics-enabled early warning systems to flag high-risk strains; ongoing public health actions include vaccines and water sanitation. Global cholera burden remains 1.3–4 million cases and up to 143,000 deaths annually.

articleSummary: Ocular toxoplasmosis, a relapsing retinal inflammation caused by Toxoplasma gondii, is a focus in Australia (Flinders University) and Brazil (University of São Paulo). articleSummary: Contagiousness of fever with rash infections peaks around rash onset rather than during peak fever. Rash reflects high pathogen levels as the immune system fights the infection. Four common rash illnesses and their transmission: Measles spreads via respiratory droplets or airborne, with the main contagious period around rash onset (about five days before and after). Chickenpox (varicella) spreads by droplets and direct contact and remains contagious from 1–2 days before rash until all lesions crust. Hand-foot-and-mouth disease (HFMD) transmits through droplets, contaminated objects, or fecal-oral routes; risk is higher about one week after rash onset. Scarlet fever (group A Streptococcus) spreads mainly by droplets, with a potentially prolonged contagious period if untreated. Prevention includes timely isolation, rigorous hand hygiene and environmental cleaning, avoiding school/work during illness, and vaccination (MMR for measles, varicella vaccine, and EV-A71 vaccine for HFMD). Beijing, China.
notes: 本記事は教育的・啓発的な公衆衛生情報記事であり、新規クラスタ発生の報告ではない。複数疾患が列挙されているが、具体的な患者数、発症状況、流行規模に関する記載がなく、シグナルトリアージの対象外。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Fight against Chikungunya outbreak in Mato Grosso do Sul's indigenous reserve gains reinforcements.
articleHeadline: Combate a surto de chikungunya em reserva indígena do MS ganha reforço
articleSummary: Chikungunya outbreak in the Dourados Indigenous Reserve, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, with reinforced response: 50 health agents join 40 SUS National Force professionals in the region since March 17; 20 of the 50 active since March 3. Teams operate within the reserve and in urban Dourados, including Itapoã. Actions include mass cleanups, elimination of Aedes aegypti breeding sites, and insecticide spraying; one mobilization visited about 250 households with four trucks of materials. Government distributes 2,000 food baskets this week, aiming for 6,000 by June. Health Ministry allocated 900,000 reais for surveillance, assistance, and control. SUS National Force has conducted over 1,400 consultations in the reserve, especially in Jaguapiru and Bororó. Dourados reports 1,314 confirmed chikungunya cases, nearly 70% in indigenous villages. Symptoms: fever, myalgia, headache, severe arthralgia. Weekly ten-minute home checks to remove breeding sites; inspect water tanks, plant trays, bottles, tires, gutters, drains, tarps, and containers.
notes: チクングニア熱はネッタイシマカ（Aedes aegypti）媒介で高い流行性を持つ。先住民保護区という脆弱集団の濃密な感染、政府による大規模資源投入（90万レアル、2,000～6,000食糧バスケット配布、40名+50名の保健職員派遣）が確認されており、対策の複雑性と必要性が高い。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Case of 300 Tons of Diseased Pork: 26 Public Schools, a Chain of Preschool Canteens Involved
articleHeadline: Vụ 300 tấn thịt lợn bệnh: 26 trường công lập, loạt bếp ăn mầm non liên quan
articleSummary: 300 tons of diseased pork trafficked in Hanoi, involving 26 public schools and numerous private preschool kitchens. Hanoi-based Industrial Catering Service Company bought pigs from Cuong Phat to supply 26 public schools and many private preschool canteens. Investigations show Cuong Phat received pork from a slaughterhouse run by Nguyen Thi Thu Hien; authorities say Cuong Phat colluded to buy cheap, sick pigs and repackage them as 'lợn sạch' before sale. Eight suspects have been indicted; four charged with food-safety violations, including Nguyen Thi Hien, Do Van Thanh, Nguyen Thi Binh, and Nguyen Van Thanh, with the director of Cuong Phat also named. The case is linked to the slaughter and sale of pigs infected with African swine fever. Over 2,900 Hanoi schools have reviewed suppliers; the Education and Training Department requires origin verification, legal/food-safety documents, and supplier compliance, with a deadline of April 10 for origin disclosure. Hanoi Chairman Vu Dai Thang ordered stronger food safety management on April 2.
notes: アフリカ豚コレラ感染豚肉の大量不正流通という食品安全危機。ハノイ市の公立学校26校と複数の保育園食堂が汚染豚肉の供給を受けた。ベトナム当局が捜査・起訴を進行中。食品安全管理の強化が指示されており、政府の関心が高い。対象国Vietnam内での事件であり、国際的拡大リスクは現時点では低い。

articleHeadline: Casos de dengue disparam quase 50% em MG em três semanas e passam de 39 mil; mortes sobem
articleSummary: Dengue cases in Minas Gerais, Brazil, climbed sharply over three weeks from March 16 to April 7, 2026, according to an epidemiological bulletin issued by SES-MG on April 6. Probable dengue rose from 26,471 to 39,551 (up 49.41%), while confirmed dengue increased from 8,144 to 13,031 (about 60%). Dengue deaths rose from 6 to 8, with 23 deaths under investigation (up from 14). Chikungunya also surged: probable cases from 4,048 to 6,493 (+~60%), and confirmed from 2,306 to 3,367; one death confirmed and two under investigation. Zika remains low, with probable cases 19 to 31 and confirmed 3 to 6; no deaths confirmed or under investigation. The data reflect ongoing transmission within Minas Gerais during early 2026.

articleSummary: COVID-19 began in Wuhan, China, with the Huanan Market identified as the first outbreak site; Wuhan endured the strictest lockdown in history. articleHeadline: Kasus Campak di Rembang Masih Nihil - Suara Merdeka Muria
articleSummary: Measles remains absent in Rembang, Indonesia, as of Monday, April 6, according to RSUD Dr. R Soetrasno Rembang. This comes amid reports of rising measles cases in several regions, but the hospital has not identified any cases in its catchment. Hospital director Dr. Samsul Anwar said authorities intensified prevention and education before and after Lebaran, focusing on early symptoms, environmental hygiene, and completing child immunizations. Families are advised to seek care promptly if fever with a widespread red rash and respiratory symptoms appear. Measles is highly contagious and can cause serious complications, especially in children under five, including dehydration requiring intensive care. No cases among toddlers have been reported in Rembang based on field surveillance and hospital data. Strengthening cooperation between health workers and parents to visit posyandu or puskesmas is key to maintaining zero-case status.

articleHeadline: La ciencia por sí sola no detendrá la fiebre de Lassa, una enfermedad grave que sigue causando muertes evitables | Tribuna
articleSummary: Lassa fever remains one of West Africa’s most persistent health threats, killing and disabling rural communities where rodent-to-human transmission occurs. Many infections go unrecognized due to non-specific febrile symptoms and limited diagnostics, with annual productivity losses in the region around $160 million. In 2024, WAHO and regional health ministries, with CEPI support, formed the Coalition Against Lassa Fever to strengthen surveillance, vaccine trial networks, data sharing, and regulatory and policy frameworks for vaccine introduction. Three vaccine candidates are in clinical development, and one could be authorized within the next decade. To translate science into protection, authorities must plan now: determine first-vaccination groups (health workers, vulnerable populations), analyze district- and season-specific risk, and design distribution plans within existing infrastructure with cost considerations. The Enable study, CEPI-funded, monitors Lassa prevalence across West Africa—the largest of its kind. Community engagement and trust-building are essential before vaccine deployment.
